verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents delivery to warehouses (ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres), object stores, "dozens of SaaS tools", and a generic webhook destination, backed by a destinations catalog page. Functions filter, transform and enrich events before they reach a destination, and routing is controlled by which sources are connected to which destinations. The catalog's size and documentation depth are only asserted, and the evidence does not show functions or mappings scoped to individual destinations. missing for 10: evidence of a large, individually documented destination catalog ("dozens" is vague), explicit per-destination field mapping configuration, explicit per-destination (per-connection) filter scoping, independent hands-on corroboration of destination breadth.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can route events to a large catalog of documented destination integrations with per-destination mapping and filtering

citations.quote: Delivery to destinations — ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres, S3, GCS, and dozens of SaaS tools, streamed or micro-batched depending on what the destination prefers.
Send data to one of those destinations with Jitsu. Learn more about destination on docs website
Send data to any HTTP endpoint. You can use this destination to send data to Slack, Discord, or any other service that accepts HTTP requests.
Filter - Exclude data that fails to meet your specified criteria. Transform - Modify data to fit the schema of your destination. Enrich - Add extra information to the event.
You can control which events become active by choosing not to connect a source to a destination or by using a Jitsu Function to filter out unwanted events before they are sent.
